title: Babel (Genesis 11:1–9)
hookLine: humans build a tower to make a name for themselves, and languages scatter
carry: no need to make a name

lines: A NAME IN LIGHTS ON A NEW TOWER.
A PLAIN IN THE LAND OF SHINAR.
cards: A ribbon cutting, a light show, a name in giant letters at the top of a new tower, so everyone driving into the city knows who built it. Building high to be seen is an old idea.

In Genesis, after the flood, people move east and settle on a plain in the land of Shinar. Some readers picture the stepped towers of baked brick, called ziggurats, whose ruins still stand in that part of the world.
Everyone speaks one language. And they have a new technology, and a big idea.

teach.h: BRICK FOR STONE, TAR FOR MORTAR.
teach.b: The technology is brick. In the King James Bible: "they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter." Slime is bitumen, tar.
Fired bricks and tar: a way to build high.

teach.h: LET US MAKE US A NAME.
teach.b: And the big idea, verse four: "let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth."
Make us a name: that's the heart of it. Not a temple to honor God. A monument to themselves, so they'd never be scattered.
And remember, after the flood, God had told Noah's family to fill the earth. They want to stay put, and be well-known.

teach.h: GOD COMES DOWN TO SEE IT.
teach.b: Then comes a line with a smile in it: "And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower." A tower meant to reach heaven, and God has to come down to see it. From heaven, it's tiny.
So God confuses their language, and they stop building, and they scatter. And the city gets its name.
In Hebrew, Babel sounds like balal, to mix up, to confuse. The text is enjoying the pun: Babel, the name of the great city Babylon, is tied here to confusion.
Some Christians read the story alongside Pentecost in the book of Acts, when the Spirit comes and people from many nations each hear the apostles in their own language.
Babel scatters the languages; Pentecost gathers people without erasing them.

teach.h: LET US MAKE US A NAME.
teach.b: And there's one more contrast, coming tomorrow: they wanted to make a name. Tomorrow, God offers to make one.

how: Some churches read the Babel story at Pentecost, alongside Acts 2, and some read the Pentecost lesson aloud in several languages at once.

to build a tower to heaven and make a name for themselves.

games.why: "let us make us a name, lest we be scattered." God had told Noah's family to fill the earth. they want to stay put, and be well-known.

practice: Notice where your day goes into making a name: the post, the reply-all, the story told so you come out well, with no judgment, just noticing.
Then think of one good thing you could do where nobody would ever know it was you, like fixing something quietly, and picture walking away from it. If you pray, you can offer it to God.

wordCard.voice: Babel. A tower meant to reach heaven, built to make a name, and the city named for what happened next: balal, mixed up.
